raising an occasion also fires a same-named declared world event; `W-BEAT-ONCE-RUN-USER` fires only on a defaulted `once`; `0.23.0`: occasion `select: sequence` presents every eligible beat in order; a scene or bundle beat's `also: true` rides along after a `select: first` winner and is ignored by `W-BEAT-SHADOWED` / `W-BEAT-PRIORITY-TIE`; bundle beats in lore documents; index beat rows carry `when` and `title` for menus; `0.22.0`: an occasion's `target:` may name a domain, `{ prefix, entity }`, so a beat target must be `<prefix>.<member>` of that `entities:` kind — `E-BEAT-ATTR` with a did-you-mean; entry beats take `once`; `pick: none` passes on a `select: all` list; new `W-BEAT-PRIORITY-TIE` and `W-BEAT-ONCE-RUN-USER`) | [0.23.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.23.0.md); [0.22.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.22.0.md); [0.21.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.21.0.md); [CHANGELOG `0.23.1`](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) |
| Play / test harness (`lute play` scripts, derivation in trace and test) | 0.22.0 (`engine:` play steps write engine-owned state and facts, reserved relations included; a script starts from a save — `visited:`, `presented:`, `quests:`, `entriesRead:` — varies `choose:` per step, fires world events with `event:`, and asserts with step and top-level `expect:`; `lute test` runs every play carrying an `expect:`; `lute trace` / `test` / `play` apply seed facts and Datalog rules by default, `derive: false` / `--no-derive` restores the `0.21` answer) | 0.23.1 (a `::end` in `lute play` ends only the presentation it runs in and a step `end: true` ends the playthrough; step `expect:` gains `quests` / `state` / `facts` / `notFacts`; a `*.test.yaml` gains `expect.facts` / `notFacts` / `eligible` and `beat:`; trace and test apply reward `credits:` and walk objective bodies as play does; `lute calendar --script` replays the script's steps; `0.23.0`: `lute beats`, `lute calendar` and `lute scenario knowledge` overviews; play presents `sequence` lists and `also` beats, gains the `presented:` expectation, snapshots `prev.run` at `newRun`, and credits rewards; trace and run raise `<occasion>@<target>` and present one bundle beat with `--beat`) | [0.23.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.23.0.md); [0.22.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.22.0.md); [CHANGELOG `0.23.1`](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) |


## Notes on the boundaries

- **`0.23.1` is a patch on the `0.23` line: no new syntax, no IR shape
  change.** A subquest whose `tier` differs from its parent's is now
  `E-QUEST-TIER-MIX`; an occasion target domain may narrow to `members:`; a
  raised occasion first fires a same-named declared world event (every active
  quest's `<on event>` handlers) and then judges its `on=` objectives, whose
  `by` deadline is judged only there, after `done`. An untagged component line
  takes the code `lute tag` would write, so its `lineId` may change once. The
  spec text is still the proposal that introduced each construct; the release
  record is the
  [changelog](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) and
  the [versioning guide](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/versioning.md).
- **`0.23.0` is additive, but a sharper checker can redden a clean
  project.** Every `0.22.0` document parses and compiles as before (only the
  version strings move); the new syntax — `by=`, objective `target=`,
  `also:`, `select: sequence`, `<beat>` in lore, `<hub prompt>`,
  `{{@p}}` string params, `prev.run.*`, `cast:`, `credits:` — is opt-in. What
  can change is `check-project`'s answer: the condition decider now proves
  same-path contradictions (`run.n > 5 && run.n < 3`, `x && !x`) dead, so a
  guard that was always false is now `E-BEAT-UNREACHABLE`,
  `E-ENTRY-UNREACHABLE`, `E-ARM-DEAD` or `E-OBJECTIVE-UNSATISFIABLE`, and a
  project that declares a cast checks its speakers.
- **`0.22.0` is breaking for compiled identity, not for grammar.** Every
  `0.21.1` document still parses and checks as before apart from the new
  diagnostics; what moves is the ids `lute compile` writes. The default
  `voiceKey` template gains `{prefix}` (the `0.21` default collided across
  documents), and a line expanded from a component gets its own
  `{prefix}.{component}#{n}.{speaker}_{code}` address. A project that recorded
  audio against the old keys pins `identity.voiceKey: "{speaker}-{code}"`;
  documents that `::use` components re-export their localization and voice
  manifests. The toolchain side changes answers too: trace and test now apply
  the project's Datalog rules by default. `<quest tier>` defaults to `user`, so
  no existing quest changes its persistence.
- **`0.21.1` is a patch on the `0.21` line: no new syntax, tighter static
  semantics.** Checks that accepted a defect and shipped the wrong thing now
  report it: `quest.<id>.state` reads as an always-assigned lifecycle enum;
  a def body passes the CEL profile gate; a def in a directive attribute folds
  to its literal or is `E-ATTR-DEF-DYNAMIC`; a `{{@def}}` that cannot be
  inlined is `E-INTERP-DEF`; `<quest>` / `<objective>` / `<on>` close their
  attributes (`E-UNKNOWN-ATTR`); a single-quoted attribute value is
  `E-ATTR-QUOTE`; an `is=` + `test=` arm covers only what both prove;
  `E-DUP-LINE-CODE` runs over expanded components; and `check-project` runs
  the compile, the single-snapshot gate (`E-CAPABILITY-MISMATCH`), and
  `E-DUP-VOICEKEY`. The spec text for these rules is still the proposal that
  introduced each construct; the release record is the
  [changelog](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) and
  the [versioning guide](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/versioning.md).
- **`0.11.0` moves the IR's `major.minor` with nothing behind it — the first
  time this stack records that shape.** `0.10.1` stayed inside `0.10` and cost
  nothing; `0.10.2` also stayed inside `0.10` but moved real content
  (`meta.plugin`); `0.11.0` moves the *number itself* out of `0.10` into
  `0.11` while carrying **zero** content or shape change — the artifact
  `0.11.0` produces is byte-identical to `0.10.2`'s. An engine gated on IR
  `0.10` still has to widen its gate to `0.11` to keep accepting artifacts
  (the runtime contract gates on `major.minor`, not on whether anything
  inside actually changed), and `schemas/lute-ir-0.10.schema.json` is renamed
  to `schemas/lute-ir-0.23.schema.json` under the `0.7.0` precedent — a
  `major.minor` move renames the schema file regardless of why it moved. The
  release itself is entirely toolchain: a new `schedule.yaml` project-file
  layer and `lute play` command (`0.21.0` removed the layer again and rebuilt
  `lute play` on occasions — [Playing a story](/tooling/play/)), plus two fixes in the
  shared reference runner (a compiled `<when is=…>` match arm now reads its
  structured `expr` instead of always falling through to `<otherwise>`, and a
  hub whose scripted decisions run out with an eligible option remaining now
  halts incomplete instead of silently converging).
- **`0.6.0` is the one breaking *grammar* revision in the current stack.** It
  removed the `persist=` attribute so `into=` alone drives the choice run-record
  sugar, and made shot headings free text. Pre-`0.6.0` documents carrying a bare
  `into=` (previously a silent no-op) now record.
- **`0.8.0` — the adoption release — is backward compatible in the grammar, but
  it is not a pure addition.** Every item in it traces to a gap found assessing
  Lute against a real 777-scene / 583-quest game catalog, and two of those items
  have edges worth naming. The IR **gains a command kind**, `end`; an unknown
  `kind` is a hard error under the execution-model version policy, so a `0.7`
  engine MUST refuse an artifact carrying one — which is the intended signal,
  since termination is capability an older engine cannot fake. And
  `E-STATE-COLLECTION` **enforces a rule that was always normative but never
  checked**: a `state:` declaration typed `list`/`record`/`map` used to pass the
  shape validator and now fails. Everything else is optional and append-only —
  apart from that one declaration, a `0.7.0`-clean document needs nothing but a
  restamped `luteVersion:` to check clean under `0.8.0`.
- **`addr` widths are uniform per artifact, and that is now a guarantee.** The
  index segment used to be a fixed four digits, so a shot with 100 or more
  records emitted `001-11500` beside `001-1400` and string comparison reported
  `"001-11500" < "001-1400"` — lexicographic order silently diverged from
  execution order. Both segments are now padded to a width computed from the
  document and held uniform across the artifact, so *lexicographic order over
  `addr` equals execution order* is something an engine may rely on. A document
  whose every shot emits fewer than 100 addresses compiles byte-identically to
  `0.7.0`. `addr` is still a position regenerated on every compile, never an
  identity — the stable joins remain `lineId` / `voiceKey`.
- **`0.9.0` — vocabulary ownership — is breaking in validation, not in
  grammar.** The compiler declares the seven content-vocabulary *slots* and
  ships **no members**, so a document writing `emotion="delighted"` needs its
  project to declare `emotion`; using a slot nobody declared is
  `E-DOMAIN-UNKNOWN`, an **error**, where `action` in particular used to be
  skipped outright. Every pre-`0.9.0` `enums:` block still parses byte-for-byte
  — a bare sequence is shorthand for `{ members: [...] }` — but a declaration of
  `action` MUST now supply `exits:` and one of `anchor` MUST supply `default:`,
  because those are the two places the compiler branches on *which* member, and
  it no longer infers them from a name prefix. **The IR shape did not move in
  that release**: no field was added, renamed, or moved, and `irVersion` read
  `"0.9.0"` only because a release re-aligns every axis — an engine gated on IR
  `0.8` had only to widen its gate to `0.9`. The
  artifact's *content* does move — `enums` becomes populated for a project that
  declares inline or through `uses:`, and `capabilityVersion` shifts. The
  authoring side is written up at [Content vocabulary](/language/vocabulary/).
- **`0.9.0` also made an imported component body check like the content it
  is.** Five of `check()`'s eighteen diagnostic stages were root-only and never
  ran over a component body, so the same lines checked *clean* through a `::use`
  and *dirty* at scene level — content-line attribute rules, `E-DUP-LINE-CODE`,
  reachability, admission of content the walker does not process, and injection
  folding. All five run now, anchored at the `::use` site with a prefix naming
  the component and its file. A component body that used to pass may report, and
  every such report was already reaching the artifact or already being silently
  dropped. What a component body still does **not** get is its own vocabulary
  scope: its `uses:` and its own inline `enums:` are both discarded at parse, so
  the body resolves vocabulary against the **importing** document.
- **`0.10.0` — the toolchain says what it knows — reddens documents, mocks, and
  the IR shape.** Thirteen language changes, and the through-line is that every
  one of them is a place the checker already held the answer. Three of them can
  redden a document that checks clean today: `::set` now types its right-hand
  side against the path it writes (`E-SET-TYPE`), the six logic tags close their
  attribute sets (`E-UNKNOWN-ATTR`, and `E-AS-REMOVED` for `as=` on a
  `<choice>`), and a `<quest start>` gate that can never open is
  `E-QUEST-UNREACHABLE` where it used to be silent. `mocks/*.yaml` is validated
  for the first time and its `file:` key is **required** — a mock without one is
  `E-MOCK-SUBJECT`. And the IR **shape** moves for the first time since
  `0.8.0`: `provenance.reason` becomes `provenance.explanation`, so an engine
  gated on IR `0.9` must widen to `0.10` and rename the one field it reads.
  `W-INJECT-CONFLICT` is **removed** rather than narrowed, and the information
  it carried is dropped, not migrated — agreement with the declared default was
  its only trigger, so there was nothing left to warn about.
- **The `0.6.1` coverage warnings are honesty, not errors.** They name the exact
  edge of what static analysis can prove — a stale `luteVersion` stamp, an
  unproducible trace mock — and never flip the exit code on their own. The third,
  `W-UNPROVEN-RELATIONAL` (a relational fact query the checker could neither prove
  nor refute), is gone since `0.20.0`: `check-project` now decides relational
  guards, reporting the dead ones through their slots' errors and the redundant
  ones as `W-FACT-GUARANTEED`, and a merely *possible* guard is the normal case
  and silent. The two `0.8.0` additions are ordinary findings rather than
  coverage claims — unreachable content after an `::end`, and a translatable
  record missing a locale the bundle declares — but they carry the same
  severity. Promote any of them to an error with `--deny <CODE>` or
  `--deny-warnings`.
- **Design rationale lives alongside the specs.** The four-tier state model's
  *why* is recorded in
  [`state-model-design.md`](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/state-model-design.md),
  a non-normative companion to `0.0.1` §9.
- **Capability surfaces are specified separately.** Character/cast identity and
  the plugin system are capability proposals, not core scenario-DSL revisions.
  The plugin system's current revision is `0.0.4`, landing alongside `0.10.2`:
  a plugin-owned, checker-validated frontmatter key now reaches the compiled
  artifact (`meta.plugin`) instead of being discarded at compile time. `0.0.3`
  — `lute.core` exports an empty `enums`, an `enums` entry may carry the long
  form's member semantics, and the closed `semantics` flag vocabulary drops
  the two flags no consumer read — and `0.0.2` — option and frontmatter value
  validation, reserved stamp-attribute rejection, cross-cutting `stampAttrs`,
  and the declarative `lower: { record, fields }` form made real — remain its
  base as amended. See the [specification index](/spec/) for all four.

---

# Specification index

Lute is specified as a **stack of versioned proposals** under [`docs/proposals/`](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/tree/main/docs/proposals). Each revision is a compatible refinement or extension of the one before, so the stack reads cumulatively: `0.1.0` is the scene kind + shared kernel, and every later revision cites it.

:::note
The **repository files are the normative source of truth.** This site is the readable companion — where the two differ, the proposal in the repo wins. The current language version is **0.23.1**.
:::

## Scenario DSL (the language)

|---|---|---|

| 0.1.0 | The language proper — scene kind + shared kernel: logic layer, Lute-CEL, scalar state model, totality, identity/i18n, and reusable content components. | [0.1.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.1.0.md) |
| 0.2.0 | Document-kind system (making `.lute` polymorphic), the `<on>` ECA trigger, the `quest.*` state tier, and the quest kind in full. | [0.2.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.2.0.md) |

| 0.5.1 | `trace` preview of quest-gated reads plus authoring-surface honesty items (delivery flags, `lute context` reserved paths, event/component diagnostics). | [0.5.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.5.1.md) |
| 0.5.2 | A single new `E-UNSET-LITERAL` diagnostic catching the most common misspelling of the *unset* sentinel in a CEL guard. | [0.5.2.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.5.2.md) |
| 0.6.0 | `into=` records without `persist=`; free shot headings — **breaking**. | [0.6.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.6.0.md) |
| 0.6.1 | Three verification-coverage warnings (`W-UNPROVEN-RELATIONAL`, `W-LUTE-VERSION-STALE`, `W-TRACE-MOCK-UNPRODUCIBLE`) and `--deny`/`--deny-warnings` warning promotion; a compatible refinement of 0.6.0. | [0.6.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.6.1.md) |
| 0.7.0 | Version unification — language, IR, and toolchain aligned at `0.7.0`; **no grammar, semantic, or IR shape change** (byte-for-byte `0.6.1` semantics). | [0.7.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.7.0.md) |
| 0.8.0 | The **adoption release**: `::end` termination, `after: active()`, the reserved `quest.<id>.activatedAt` anchor, scalar-only author `state:`, `Artifact.shots`, the localization round trip, `identity:` templates, and a uniform-width `addr`; every item traces to a gap found assessing Lute against a real 777-scene / 583-quest game catalog. | [0.8.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.8.0.md) |
| 0.9.0 | **Vocabulary ownership**: the compiler declares the seven content-vocabulary *slots* (`emotion`, `action`, `anchor`, `mood`, `volume`, `musicAction`, `vfxType`) and ships **no members**, so every member is the project's, declared inline, in a schema reached through `uses:`, or by a plugin's `enums` export; the `enums:` long form's `exits:`/`default:` carries the member semantics two hardcoded name heuristics used to guess; using a slot nobody declared is `E-DOMAIN-UNKNOWN` instead of silently unchecked; and five root-only check stages now run over imported component bodies. **Breaking** for documents that use a slot. The IR re-aligned to `0.9.0` and was shape-identical to `0.8.0`. | [0.9.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.9.0.md) |
| 0.10.0 | **the toolchain says what it knows**: thirteen changes, each closing a place where the checker held the answer and did not say it. `::set` types its right-hand side against the path it writes (`E-SET-TYPE`); the six logic tags close their attribute sets (`E-UNKNOWN-ATTR`, `E-AS-REMOVED`); a quest gate that can never open is an error and a contradictory objective pair is `E-OBJECTIVE-CONTRADICTION`; `lute.project.yaml` gains `defaults:`; nested manifests are validated by every command that walks them; `mocks/*.yaml` is checked and requires `file:`; timeline time is integer milliseconds; four new warnings land and `W-INJECT-CONFLICT` is **removed** because its only trigger was agreement. **Breaking** for documents (§§3, 4, 5) and for mocks. The **IR shape changes for the first time since `0.8.0`** — `provenance.reason` becomes `provenance.explanation`, so an engine gated on IR `0.9` must widen to `0.10`. | [0.10.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.10.0.md) |
| 0.10.1 | **alignment only**: no grammar production, no static-semantic rule, no IR shape change; `0.10.0` semantics byte for byte. The release's two fixes are toolchain — `lute test` gains `--project` so a document that reaches its schema or its directives through a manifest can be tested at all, and an `assetKind` segment declared with a `Type` outside the closed segment production is rejected at plugin load instead of enforcing nothing. Written down because a language version absent from this stack cannot be told apart from one nobody recorded. | [0.10.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.10.1.md) |
| 0.10.2 | **Alignment only on the language axis; the IR axis is not**: no grammar production, no static-semantic rule (`0.10.1`/`0.10.0` semantics byte for byte). The release is one IR/toolchain change — a plugin-owned, checker-validated frontmatter key now reaches the compiled artifact (`meta.plugin`) instead of being discarded at compile time (plugin-system `0.0.4`). Additive only: no engine gate widens, since `0.10.2` shares major.minor `0.10` with `0.10.0`/`0.10.1`. | [0.10.2.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.10.2.md) |
| 0.11.0 | **Alignment only, on BOTH axes**: no grammar production, no static-semantic rule, no IR shape or content change (`0.10.2`/`0.10.1`/`0.10.0` semantics byte for byte). The release is entirely toolchain — a `schedule.yaml` project-file layer and `lute play`, a whole-project chained-playthrough command with `--coverage` review-gap reporting, plus two shared-reference-runner fixes. Under the then-current `major.minor` gate this one was not free for a consuming engine: `0.10` → `0.11` crossed the gated line, so the schema file was renamed under the `0.7.0` precedent (published today as `lute-ir-0.23.schema.json`). | [0.11.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.11.0.md) |
| 0.11.1 | `<branch>` gains two optional attributes: `prompt="…"` (the situation sentence a host UI shows above the option labels, `E-BRANCH-PROMPT`) and `timeout="N"` (a positive-integer seconds budget, `E-BRANCH-TIMEOUT`). IR additive-only: `prompt`/`timeoutSec` on the choice record, omitted when unauthored. *Backfilled 2026-08-26 — shipped 2026-08-19 with its record only in the changelog.* | [0.11.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.11.1.md) |
| 0.12.0 | **Forward jumps**: `::mark{id=…}` / content-line `id=…` label a position; `::next{to=… when=…}` jumps to it, forward-only, so the walk stays a DAG. New diagnostics `E-MARK-DUP`, `E-NEXT-UNDEFINED`, `E-NEXT-BACKWARD`, `W-CODE-AFTER-NEXT`. IR is a pure restamp (`::next` lowers to the existing `jump`/`match` records); `lute.core` gains `mark`/`next`, so `capabilityVersion` moves. | [0.12.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.12.0.md) |
| 0.13.0 | **Code lock**: one new universal frontmatter key, `codesLocked:`, marking a document's line codes as published identity; `lute tag --force` renumbers drafts in clean document order and refuses locked documents (fail-closed). Ships alongside the toolchain's lint layer (`lute lint`, `lute.lint.yaml`, plugin `lints` exports) and relaxes the runtime version gate to **MAJOR-only** (minor/patch compatible-by-default). IR is a pure restamp. | [0.13.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.13.0.md) |
| 0.14.0 | **Subquests**: `<objective quest="childId"/>` makes a child quest's completion a parent objective. Completion and upward failure are compiler-synthesized (`done` = `quest.<child>.state == 'complete'`; parent `fail` gains one `failed` test per required child); downward failure (terminal parent fails still-`active` children) and referenced-child activation (no `start` → activates with the parent; a `start` is evaluated only while the parent is active) are engine rules. Project shape is a tree, not a DAG — `E-OBJECTIVE-QUEST-DONE`, `E-QUEST-REF-UNKNOWN`, `E-QUEST-MULTI-PARENT`, `E-QUEST-TREE-CYCLE`, plus `E-OBJECTIVE-UNSATISFIABLE` propagation from an unreachable child. IR additive-only: `ObjectiveEntry.quest`, omitted when unauthored. | [0.14.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.14.0.md) |
| 0.15.0 | **Authored scene identity**: one new scene frontmatter key, `id:`, becomes the canonical scene key everywhere the derived `{character}.{episodeId}` join is consumed today (lineId prefix, `visited()`/connectivity, `prereqEdges`, `project.index.json`, the runtime visited-set), and demotes the four legacy identity keys (`character`/`season`/`episode`/`episodeId`) to optional when present; a second new frontmatter key, `extra:`, lands on scene and quest roots as a free descriptive block (open mapping of scalars or flat scalar-lists, carried verbatim into `meta.extra`, read by no language rule). Three new diagnostics `E-META-ID`/`E-META-VALUE`/`W-META-LEGACY`, `E-META-MISSING` narrowed to fire only when merged frontmatter lacks `id:`, and `E-CONN-EPISODE-ID-DUP`'s message generalised to name the *canonical scene id*. IR additive-only under `0.13.0`'s MAJOR-only gate: `SceneMeta.id` required, the four legacy identity fields optional, `extra` on both `SceneMeta` and `QuestMeta`. | [0.15.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.15.0.md) |
| 0.15.1 | **Alignment only, on BOTH axes**: no grammar production, no static-semantic rule, no IR shape or content change (`0.15.0` semantics byte for byte). The release is entirely toolchain — the npm distribution ships `lute-lsp` alongside `lute` (a second `bin` launcher entry, both binaries carried in each per-platform core package), so downstream editors can spawn the language server through the same `@lute-lang/lute` install the CLI already uses. `schemas/lute-ir-0.15.schema.json` keeps its name and `$id`; no engine gate widens under `0.13.0`'s MAJOR-only runtime contract. | [0.15.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.15.1.md) |
| 0.16.0 | **Declarative rewards**: one new self-closing element, `<reward kind= target= amount= when= on=/>`, legal only as a direct child of `<quest>` or `<objective>`, with `amount` admitting an integer scalar (negatives real) or the new range literal `N..M`; lowers to pure data on the owning records (`QuestCmd.rewards` / `ObjectiveEntry.rewards`) — the engine grants, the reference runtime never rolls a range. Two new diagnostics `E-REWARD-ATTR` (shape) and `E-REWARD-KIND` (vocabulary, only when a plugin declares `rewardKinds:`); `reward.when` joins the CEL-slot registry. `lute run` / `play` / `trace` emit deterministic `grant` transcript events at each fresh transition (spec §3 D-D — objective grants precede quest grants, all grants precede the corresponding lifecycle handler body). A plugin manifest MAY export a `rewardKinds:` vocabulary; folded into the capability snapshot as a guarded, sorted section so `capabilityVersion` moves only for projects that declare kinds. IR additive-only under `0.13.0`'s MAJOR-only gate: both `rewards` arrays are `skip-when-empty`, so a rewardless artifact stays byte-identical to `0.15.1` output. The tree-sitter grammar gains the `reward` production. | [0.16.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.16.0.md) |
| 0.16.1 candidate | **Prospective tooling only; not released.** A checked continuation compiler appends ordinary final-shot body source to a frozen scene template and emits full ordinary artifact snapshots per complete accepted unit; `lute compile-stream` exposes the same contract as flushed NDJSON. No new grammar, permission, runtime effect, or IR patch shape. Each unit recompiles cumulative source through the existing compiler, and snapshot consumers retain their numeric cursor/state/facts while rebuilding address lookup. | [0.16.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.16.1.md) |
| 0.17.0 | **Checked continuations and least-authority compilation**: the toolchain adds the append-only checked continuation compiler and `lute compile-stream`, plus generic capability-permission ceilings for directives, state and fact writes, bridges, rewards, and quests. Both reuse the existing language and ordinary artifact contract, so language and IR are alignment restamps with no grammar, static-semantic, or IR-shape change. | [0.17.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.17.0.md) |
| `0.17.1` | Alignment-only release: no grammar production, static-semantic rule, or IR shape/content change (`0.17.0` semantics byte for byte). The release is repository hygiene — example cast/project identifiers renamed to neutral same-length names, a non-normative adoption assessment dropped. `schemas/lute-ir-0.17.schema.json` keeps its name and `$id`. | [0.17.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.17.1.md) |
| `0.17.2` | **Additive plugin owner metadata**: passthrough `kind: "plugin"` records may carry the resolved owning plugin id in optional `plugin` metadata, so hosts can dispatch by `(plugin, tag)`; declarative presentation directives with `lower: { record, fields }` continue to emit stable core records. No grammar or static-semantic change; `schemas/lute-ir-0.17.schema.json` keeps its name and `$id`. | [0.17.2.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.17.2.md) |
| `0.18.0` | **Range patterns in `<when is>`**: inclusive numeric range literals `N..M` / `N..` / `..M` (signed decimal bounds) join the `is=` literal set, and a subject declared `number` becomes a coverage-checkable domain — interval union over the reals, so `E-NONEXHAUSTIVE` names the first uncovered gap and `E-ARM-DEAD` / `W-OVERLAP-ARMS` / `W-OTHERWISE-DEAD` are interval-aware. New `E-WHEN-RANGE` (a malformed or empty range) and `W-WHEN-TEST-LITERAL` (a literal-comparison `test` guard that `is=` expresses; its `migrate` fixit is applied by `lute fix`). IR is an alignment restamp — range arms lower to the existing `>=` / `<=` / `&&` operators — and the schema renames to `schemas/lute-ir-0.18.schema.json`. | [0.18.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.18.0.md) |
| `0.19.0` | **Lore entries (queried content)**: a third document kind, `kind: lore`, whose top level is a set of `<entry id target category title series order when>` declarations — content the engine looks up (item descriptions, found notes, inscriptions, codex pages, barks) instead of plays. Entry bodies admit content lines, `<match>`, `::set`, `::assert`, `::retract`; knowledge is revealed with plain `::assert`; the reserved engine-written `entry.<id>.read` path gates series and scenes; effects apply on the first read only. Quest and lore documents may declare a document `id:` (the bundle name), and a lore document a `series:` ordered by file position. New `E-ENTRY-ATTR`, `E-ENTRY-ID-DUP`, `E-ENTRY-SERIES-ORDER`, `W-ENTRY-REF-UNKNOWN`; `lute trace`/`run --entry`, `lute lore`. IR is additive — artifact `kind: "lore"` with `LoreMeta`, the `entry` record, `QuestMeta.id`, `ProjectIndex.entries` — and the schema renames to `schemas/lute-ir-0.19.schema.json`. | [0.19.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.19.0.md) |
| `0.20.0` | **Fact envelopes (knowledge analysis)**: static semantics only, no grammar change. `check-project` decides every relational query (`holds(…)`, `count(…)`) in every guard slot as **impossible**, **guaranteed**, or **possible** from a project-wide, argument-level *may* set (every ground fact any seed, live assert, rule, or reserved relation can produce) and a path-sensitive *must* set (the monotone facts true on every route to the slot, within a document and across the `after:` graph; guards are assumptions inside their regions; `count` is decided over an interval). Dead relational guards reuse each slot's existing code (`E-ARM-DEAD`, `E-OBJECTIVE-UNSATISFIABLE`, `E-QUEST-UNREACHABLE`, `W-OBJECTIVE-HIDDEN`); new `E-ENTRY-UNREACHABLE` (a lore entry `when` that never holds — also scalar-decided in single-file `check`) and `W-FACT-GUARANTEED` (a redundant relational guard); `W-UNPROVEN-RELATIONAL` is **removed**. `lute scenario … envelope` lists the guaranteed facts at a node. IR is an alignment restamp and the schema renames to `schemas/lute-ir-0.20.schema.json`. | [0.20.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.20.0.md) |
| `0.21.0` | **Beats and occasions (story selection)**: a project names **occasions** — engine moments at which a story beat may be chosen (a hub visit, entering a room, talking to an NPC) — and a scene or lore entry becomes a **beat** by answering one: scene frontmatter `on:` / `target:` / `when:` / `priority:` / `once: run \| user \| false`, entry attributes `on=` / `priority=`. A beat is eligible when its `after:` and `when` hold and its `once` is unspent; eligible beats order by priority, then project order. A plugin may export `occasions:` (`select: first \| all`, `target: true`); occasion names are shape-only until one does. New `E-BEAT-ATTR`, `E-OCCASION-UNKNOWN`, `E-BEAT-UNREACHABLE`, `W-BEAT-SHADOWED`. `schedule.yaml` and every `E-SCHED-*` / `W-SCHED-*` code are **removed**; `lute play` is rebuilt on raised occasions and drives quest lifecycles. IR additive — `SceneMeta.beat`, `EntryCmd.on` / `priority`, `ProjectIndex.beats` — and the schema renames to `schemas/lute-ir-0.21.schema.json`. | [0.21.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.21.0.md) |
| `0.21.1` | **Patch: no silent wrong answers**. No new syntax; static semantics tighten so checks that accepted a defect now report it — `quest.<id>.state` reads as an always-assigned lifecycle enum (`W-QUEST-STATE-ISSET`), def bodies pass the CEL profile gate, a def in a directive attribute folds to its literal or is `E-ATTR-DEF-DYNAMIC`, an un-inlinable `{{@def}}` is `E-INTERP-DEF`, `<quest>` / `<objective>` / `<on>` close their attributes, a single-quoted attribute value is `E-ATTR-QUOTE`, and `check-project` runs the compile, the single-snapshot gate (`E-CAPABILITY-MISMATCH`), and the new `E-DUP-VOICEKEY` (a multi-scene project on the default voice-key template pins `identity.voiceKey: "{prefix}.{speaker}-{code}"`). The IR change is additive — a `ref` placeholder carries optional `expr`, the def body inlined — and `schemas/lute-ir-0.21.schema.json` keeps its name and `$id`. | [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md); [versioning.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/versioning.md) |
| `0.22.0` | **A reference player that can stand in for the engine**: `lute play` scripts write what the engine owns with `engine:` steps (declared state as a literal or `{ add: n }`, facts and retractions of any declared relation, reserved ones included; `newRun: { state, facts }`), start from a save (`visited:`, `presented: { run, user }`, `quests:`, `entriesRead: { run, user }`), take a per-step `choose:`, fire world events (`event:`), pass on a `select: all` list (`pick: none`), and assert with step `expect: { winner, offered, notOffered }` and a top-level `expect:`; `lute test` runs every play carrying an `expect:`, and `lute trace` / `test` / `play` apply the project's seed facts and Datalog rules by default (`derive: false` / `--no-derive` restores the `0.21` model; `lute play --explain <atom>`). Run boundaries: `<quest tier="run">` resets at a new run, entry beats take `once="run" \| "user"`, and the reserved user-tier `entry.<id>.everRead` survives every run. A `state:` declaration may be `owner: engine` (`E-ENGINE-OWNED-WRITE`); an occasion's `target:` may name a domain `{ prefix, entity }` (`E-BEAT-ATTR` outside it); `W-STAGE-ABSENT` follows paths; new warnings `W-QUEST-HANDLER-DEAD`, `W-BEAT-PRIORITY-TIE`, `W-BEAT-ONCE-RUN-USER`. **Breaking for compiled ids**: the default `voiceKey` becomes `{prefix}.{speaker}-{code}` (pin `identity.voiceKey: "{speaker}-{code}"` to keep the old keys) and a component line is addressed `{prefix}.{component}#{n}.{speaker}_{code}`. IR additive — `QuestCmd.tier`, `EntryCmd.once` — and the schema renames to `schemas/lute-ir-0.22.schema.json` (since renamed). | [0.22.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.22.0.md) |
| `0.23.0` | **Author overviews and time**: `lute beats` prints each occasion's beat ladder with the `check-project` verdicts, `lute calendar` evaluates play's own eligibility over a grid of state values (`--axis run.day=1..7 --axis run.slot=…`) from a save, and `lute scenario knowledge` traces every fact-guarded condition to its producers; `<objective by="…">` fails an objective the first time its deadline holds and `<objective on target>` judges it only for that target; occasion `select: sequence` presents every eligible beat and a beat's `also: true` rides along after a `select: first` winner; a lore document may bundle scene-like `<beat>` blocks (canonical id `<document id>.<beat id>`); `<hub prompt>`; component `string` params interpolate as `{{@p}}`; the reserved read-only `prev.run.<path>`; a declared cast makes an unknown speaker `E-CAST-UNKNOWN`; a reward kind may `credits:` a state path (`W-REWARD-DOUBLE-CREDIT`); the condition decider reasons per path across `&&` / `||`, so contradictions that used to pass are errors, and `check-project --wip` softens the ones caused by unwritten content. IR additive — a `beat` record, `BeatIr.also`, `ObjectiveEntry.by` / `target`, `HubCmd.prompt`, `RewardEntry.credits`, index beat rows' `bundle` kind, `when` and `title` — and the schema renames to `schemas/lute-ir-0.23.schema.json`. | [0.23.0.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.23.0.md) |
| **0.23.1** | Current tip — **Patch: trace, test and play agree**. No new syntax and no IR shape change; static semantics tighten — a subquest whose `tier` differs from its parent's is `E-QUEST-TIER-MIX`, a match arm narrows its subject so reads after an arm that takes every unset value are no longer `E-MAYBE-UNSET`, a negation over a stably derived fact is decided, and `W-BEAT-ONCE-RUN-USER` fires only on a defaulted `once`. An occasion target domain may narrow to `members:`. Runtime answers move: a raised occasion first fires a same-named declared world event (every active quest's `<on event>` handlers) and then judges its `on=` objectives, whose `by` deadline is judged only there, after `done`; an untagged component line takes the code `lute tag` would write, so its `lineId` may change once. Tooling: a `::end` in `lute play` ends only its presentation (a step `end: true` ends the play), trace and test apply reward `credits:` and objective bodies, and `lute calendar --script` replays the script. `schemas/lute-ir-0.23.schema.json` keeps its name and `$id`. | [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md); [versioning.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/versioning.md) |

| — | State-model design rationale & audit record — *why* the four-tier (`scene`/`run`/`user`/`app`) state model is shaped this way; non-normative companion to `0.0.1` §9. | [state-model-design.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/state-model-design.md) |

For the authoring-side reading of the seven vocabulary slots — the three declaration
routes and their precedence, and the `exits:`/`default:` long form — see
[Content vocabulary](/language/vocabulary/).

## Capability proposals

| Proposal | Scope | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin system 0.0.1 | Normative formats and semantics of the capability/plugin system — plugin packages, YAML manifest schemas, resolution, the capability snapshot, and the data↔code boundary. | [plugin-system/0.0.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/plugin-system/0.0.1.md) |
| Plugin system 0.0.2 | Delta on 0.0.1 — plugin option and frontmatter value validation, reserved stamp-attribute rejection, cross-cutting `stampAttrs` admissible on every directive and content line, and the declarative `lower: { record, fields }` form implemented. | [plugin-system/0.0.2.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/plugin-system/0.0.2.md) |
| Plugin system 0.0.3 | Delta on 0.0.1/0.0.2, landing with dsl 0.9.0 — `lute.core` exports an **empty** `enums`, an `enums` entry may use the long form carrying member semantics (`members`/`default`/`exits`), and the closed `semantics` flag vocabulary drops the two flags no consumer read (`isStateful`, `cancelsPrevious`), twelve → ten. | [plugin-system/0.0.3.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/plugin-system/0.0.3.md) |
| Plugin system 0.0.4 | Delta on 0.0.1/0.0.2/0.0.3, landing with dsl `0.10.2` — a plugin-owned, checker-validated top-level frontmatter key (`E-FRONTMATTER-SCHEMA`) now reaches the compiled artifact's `meta.plugin` instead of being discarded at compile time; deterministic (key-sorted), defense-in-depth re-validated against the snapshot regardless of which `CheckResult` gate produced the artifact. | [plugin-system/0.0.4.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/plugin-system/0.0.4.md) |

| Plugin system 0.0.5 | Delta on 0.0.1–0.0.4, landing with dsl `0.13.0` — the advisory `lints` export kind: declarative CEL lint rules (`lints/*.yaml`, namespaced `<plugin-id>/<rule-id>`), loaded for the lint engine and **excluded** from the capability snapshot and `capabilityVersion`, so editorial policy never moves artifact identity. | [plugin-system/0.0.5.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/plugin-system/0.0.5.md) |
| Plugin system 0.0.6 candidate | **Prospective; not released.** Delta on 0.0.1–0.0.5 adding generic project/host capability-permission ceilings for directives, state/fact writes, bridges, rewards, and quests; conjunctive project/profile/host layering; `--permission-profile`; shared checker/compiler/LSP/context enforcement; and restrictive-policy capability hashing without changing policy-free hashes. Compile-time admission only—no runtime sandbox or reward implementation. | [plugin-system/0.0.6.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/plugin-system/0.0.6.md) |
| Plugin system 0.0.7 | Delta on 0.0.1–0.0.6 — passthrough plugin IR records may carry the resolved owner id in optional `plugin` metadata; hosts dispatch by `(plugin, tag)`, while declarative presentation directives still lower to stable core records. Older artifacts without the field remain valid. | [0.0.7.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/plugin-system/0.0.7.md) |
| Character & cast 0.0.1 | The language contract for character identity, display label, costume, name-reveal, and voice-join — as a capability plugin (registry, `cast:` frontmatter, `scene.cast.*` state, resolution, `seal`/`reveal`/`wear`). | [character-cast/0.0.1.md](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/character-cast/0.0.1.md) |

The plugin system also carries a human-facing overview at [`docs/plugin-system.md`](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/plugin-system.md), and the character/cast capability its design rationale at [`character-cast/design.md`](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/character-cast/design.md).
